rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Under Sibawayh, the مصدرية أن before a command conveys both command and nominal force; grammarians mean that its imperative sense shifts into a nominal one.
rows.anchor: إذ يسوغ دخول ( أن ) المصدرية على فعل الأمر فتفيد الأمر والمصدرية معا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أن أقيموا may coordinate with لنسلم through an omitted باء, or with لنسلم understood as بأن نسلم; the latter follows Arabic coordination by meaning and is illustrated by 63:10.
rows.anchor: وإما عطف على معنى { لنسلم } لأنه وقع في موقع بأن نسلم ، كما تقدم عن الزجاج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أن is more clearly explanatory: أمرنا implies speech, so it introduces what they were told, and the coordinated command means إقامة الصلاة with an understood verb.
rows.anchor: وأظهر من هذا أن تكون ( أن ) تفسيرية . وهي تفسير لما دلت عليه واو العطف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: اتقوه coordinates with أقيموا under the same syntactic analyses; its pronoun refers to the Lord of the worlds, either as the command to believers or as indirect rendering of اتقون, as in 5:117.
rows.anchor: والضمير المنصوب عائد إلى { رب العالمين } وهو من الكلام الذي أمروا بمقتضاه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: فلما جن branches from the showing of the heavenly kingdom in 6:75, since the star belongs to that kingdom and فاء signals close derivation; al-Zamakhshari’s link to 6:74 with an intervening parenthesis is inelegant.
rows.anchor: لأن العطف بالفاء يستدعي مزيد الاتصال بين المعطوف والمعطوف عليه لما في معنى الفاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: جن عليه الليل means darkness enveloped Ibrahim, implying he was outdoors beneath the sky rather than inside a house.
rows.anchor: أي كان إبراهيم محوطا بظلمة الليل ، وهو يقتضي أنه كان تحت السماء ولم يكن في بيت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording يا قوم implies Ibrahim was traveling with a group of his people as they watched the celestial bodies; his Chaldean people were Sabians who worshiped stars and their images.
rows.anchor: أنه كان سائرا مع فريق من قومه يشاهدون الكواكب ، وقد كان قوم إبراهيم صابئين يعبدون الكواكب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: جن عليه الليل intensifies the covering image, as though the darkness were a garment; the author says جن الليل was not used intransitively to mean simply that night became dark.
rows.anchor: وهذا يقصد به المبالغة في الستر بالظلمة حتى صارت كأنها غطاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibrahim likely noticed a bright, prominent star incidentally, perhaps shining near mid-sky; alternatively, the text may omit his deliberate looking, as 26:63 omits the striking of the sea.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون نظر الكواكب فرأى كوكبا فيكون في الكلام إيجاز حذف مثل

rows.speaker: زيد بن علي
rows.claim: Zayd ibn Ali identifies the star as Venus.
rows.anchor: فعن زيد بن علي أن الكوكب هو الزهرة

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi identifies the star as Jupiter.
rows.anchor: وعن السدي أنه المشتري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause رأى كوكبا is the جواب of لما.
rows.anchor: وجملة { رأى كوكبا } جواب { لما } . والكوكب : النجم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: قال هذا ربي begins a new explanatory sentence answering the question prompted by the report that Ibrahim saw a star.
rows.anchor: وجملة : { قال هذا ربي } مستأنفة استئنافا بيانيا جوابا لسؤال ينشأ عن مضمون جملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The demonstrative marks something sought and investigated, then found; the author also allows its literal pointing and allusive sense together, comparing other Qur'anic uses.
rows.anchor: أن يكون القصد الأصلي منه هو الكناية بالإشارة عن كون المشار إليه أمرا مطلوبا مبحوثا عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Definite هذا ربي implies restriction: Ibrahim provisionally left one of their gods in place, feigning acceptance of one deity so his people would listen and move toward monotheism.
rows.anchor: فدل على أن إبراهيم عليه السلام أراد استدراج قومه فابتدأ بإظهار أنه لا يرى تعدد الآلهة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: قال is literal speech addressed to others, as shown by the passage’s sequence, its direct address يا قوم, and the fact that refuting stars alone works only if they were his people’s claimed gods; Ibrahim argued before a gathered group.
rows.anchor: فدل ذلك كله على أن إبراهيم عليه السلام قال ذلك على سبيل المجادلة لقومه وإرخاء العنان لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: هذا ربي means my creator and manager, therefore one deserving worship; Ibrahim said it hypothetically in his people’s terms to draw them in before refuting their belief.
rows.anchor: وقوله : { هذا ربي } أي خالقي ومدبري فهو مستحق عبادتي . قاله على سبيل الفرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though it sounds like disbelief, Ibrahim could utter it without believing it if he judged this the likeliest way to guide and save his people; coerced denial with a faithful heart is an analogy, and revelation may have authorized his strategy.
rows.anchor: ساغ له التصريح به لقصد الوصول إلى الحق وهو لا يعتقده ، ولا يزيد قوله هذا قومه كفرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage indicates Chaldean Sabian star worship; their idols may have represented stars, as in ancient Greek myths, or they may have worshiped stars alongside lesser images, as Greeks distinguished gods from demigods; Sabians assigned spirits to stars.
rows.anchor: وعلى هذا فالآية تقتضي أن قومه يعبدون الكواكب وأنهم على دين الصابئة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أفل means a celestial light disappeared by setting behind the horizon through the earth’s daily rotation; it is not used when the sun or star is hidden by clouds.
rows.anchor: وهو المغيب الذي يكون بغروب الكوكب وراء الأفق بسبب الدورة اليومية للكرة الأرضية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أحب here means approve or want: Ibrahim did not approve of, or want, a setting body as a deity, as established by هذا ربي; al-Zamakhshari instead supplies an omitted object, worship of those that set.
rows.anchor: الحب فيه بمعنى الرضى والإرادة ، أي لا أرضى بالآفل إلها ، أو لا أريد الآفل إلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rational masculine plural الآفلين reflects Ibrahim’s people’s belief that stars are intelligent agents governing the universe, since a worshiped being must know.
rows.anchor: بناء على اعتقاد قومه أن الكواكب عاقلة متصرفة في الأكوان ، ولا يكون الموجود معبودا إلا وهو عالم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Setting disqualifies a star because a deity must continuously oversee servants, while the absent star cannot attend to their needs; Ibrahim argues from his people’s view that setting means absence from this world.
rows.anchor: أن ما يغيب لا يستحق أن يتخذ إلها لأنه لا يغني عن عباده فيما يحتاجونه حين مغيبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The argument is not that change disproves divinity: his people did not accept that entailment, and setting is only an appearance to observers while the star remains in its orbit and returns.
rows.anchor: ولأن الأفول ليس بتغير في ذات الكوكب بل هو عرض للأبصار المشاهدة له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He argues from setting rather than rising because the earlier setting was not witnessed, making the point shorter than explaining that the rising star had previously set.
rows.anchor: فكان الأفول أخصر في الاحتجاج من أن يقول : إن هذا البازغ كان من قبل آفلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The moon’s rising is elided before لما رأى القمر, yielding فلما طلع القمر فلما رآه بازغا; this implies it rose after the star set, perhaps late at night before sunrise, and the repeated noun replaces an omitted pronoun.
rows.anchor: والتقدير : فطلع القمر فلما رآه بازغا ، فحذفت الجملة للإيجاز وهو يقتضي أن القمر طلع بعد أفول الكوكب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: بازغا means beginning to shine or rise.
rows.anchor: والبازغ : الشارق في ابتداء شروقه ، والبزوغ ابتداء الشروق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Definite هذا ربي argues that if divinity follows brightness, the moon’s greater light makes it more deserving than the star; the demonstrative alludes to finding what was sought.
rows.anchor: أفاد بتعريف الجزأين أنه أكثر ضوءا من الكوكب فإذا كان استحقاق الإلهية بسبب النور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The demonstrative’s allusive force is to mark the object of a search as having been found.
rows.anchor: وهو كون المشار إليه مطلوبا مبحوثا عنه كما تقدم آنفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: اجتبينا means selecting and choosing; its derivation from جبي, gathering, is intensive because what is gathered is desired, like collecting tax or water in a basin.
rows.anchor: والاجتباء الاصطفاء والاختيار ، قالوا هو مشتق من الجبي ، وهو الجمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God chose these people as recipients of His guidance because He knows best where to place His message, prophethood, and guidance.
rows.anchor: والمعنى : أن الله اختارهم فجعلهم موضع هديه لأنه أعلم حيث يجعل رسالته ونبوءته وهديه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated mention of guidance reinforces their guidance; the straight path evokes a purposeful traveler reaching perfection without hesitation, bewilderment, or error, with part of the simile standing for its whole scene.
rows.anchor: فبين أنه هدى إلى صراط مستقيم ، أي إلى ما به نوال ما يعمل أهل الكمال لنواله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The straight path is monotheism and faith in foundational virtues shared by the revealed laws; the praise also indirectly reproaches the polytheists, as the next verse confirms.
rows.anchor: والصراط المستقيم هو التوحيد والإيمان بما يجب الإيمان به من أصول الفضائل التي اشتركت فيها الشرائع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is a clarifying resumption: do not wonder that some were guided while others strayed; هدى summarizes the three prior acts of guidance, especially the straight-path clause in 6:87.
rows.anchor: استئناف بياني ، أي لا تعجبوا من هديهم وضلال غيرهم . والإشارة إلى الهدى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The demonstrative makes guidance seem visible and distinctly marked, while calling it God’s guidance honors it and declares it free of error, in contrast to the polytheists’ supposed guidance from chiefs such as Amr ibn Luhayy and soothsayers.
rows.anchor: وقد زاد اسم الإشارة اهتماما بشأن الهدي إذ جعل كالشيء المشاهد فزيد باسم الإشارة كمال تمييز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse is a rhetorical summary of repeated discussion of guidance; Hatim al-Ta'i’s poem similarly gathers earlier praise in فذلك.
rows.anchor: وقد جاء هذا الكلام على طريقة الفذلكة لأحوال الهداية التي تكرر ذكرها كأبيات حاتم الطائي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: يهدي به من يشاء is circumstantial; those God wills are the chosen receptive to guidance, who reject stubbornness and pursue good until they receive revelation, divine enabling, or truthful inspiration. Its open wording invites people to seek guidance and alludes to Meccan envy of Muhammad.
rows.anchor: والمراد ب { من يشاء } الذين اصطفاهم الله واجتباهم وهو أعلم بهم وباستعدادهم لهديه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional is circumstantial: shirk destroys the reward even of people with extraordinary good works; حبط means that the reward is lost, as in 2:217.
rows.anchor: و ( حبط ) معناه تلف ، أي بطل ثوابه . وقد تقدم في قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The introduction of those given scripture, wisdom, and prophethood is a second rhetorical summary, now gathering the guided people after the first gathered guidance itself; the demonstrative singles them out, including those listed in 6:87.
rows.anchor: استئناف ابتدائي للتنويه بهم ، فهي فذلكة ثانية ، لأن الفذلكة الأولى راجعة إلى ما في الجمل السابقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الكتاب is generic for scriptures; revealed material counts as a book because it is the sort of thing meant to be written, whether or not it was written down.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالكتاب الجنس : أي الكتب . وإيتاء الكتاب يكون بإنزال ما يكتب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an says Abraham had scrolls, and Jesus had speech written in the Gospel.
rows.anchor: وقد نص القرآن على أن إبراهيم كانت له صحف بقوله : { صحف إبراهيم وموسى } ( الأعلى : 19 ) وكان لعيسى كلامه الذي كتب في الإنجيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: David received God's communicated speech as a prophet though not a messenger, while Solomon had Proverbs, the Great Compilation, and the Song of Songs, each ascribed to divine ordinances.
rows.anchor: ولداوود الكلام الصادر منه تبليغا عن الله تعالى ، وكان نبيئا ولم يكن رسولا ، ولسليمان الأمثال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author reports a tradition that Idris wrote wisdom in scrolls; Israelites call him Enoch, Egyptians Thoth, and sages Hermes.
rows.anchor: ويقال : إن إدريس كتب الحكمة في صحف وهو الذي يسميه الإسرائليون ( أخنوخ )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الحكم means wisdom, knowing paths to good and warding off harm, as with Yahya in 19:12; it may instead mean judging rightly, as for David and Solomon in 21:79.
rows.anchor: والحكم هو الحكمة ، أي العلم بطرق الخير ودفع الشر . قال تعالى في شأن يحيى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Scripture, wisdom, and prophethood were distributed: messengers and prophets who judged people could receive all three, while non-messenger prophets and righteous non-prophets received some, given the broad reference to ancestors, descendants, and siblings.
rows.anchor: وإيتاء هذه الثلاث على التوزيع ، فمنهم من أوتي جميعها وهم الرسل منهم والأنبياء الذين حكموا بين الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The فاء links the conditional to the preceding description because the earlier story from Abraham onward discredited shirk by showing that virtuous people rejected it; the transition is rhetorically apt.
rows.anchor: لأن الغرض من الجمل السابقة من قوله { وإذ قال إبراهيم لأبيه آزر } ( الأنعام : 74 ) هو تشويه أمر الشرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun بها refers to scripture, wisdom, and prophethood; هؤلاء points to the Meccan polytheists mentally present to the audience, like demonstratives in the grave-question report and al-Ahnaf’s Bukhari report about Ali.
rows.anchor: وضمير { بها } عائد إلى المذكورات : الكتاب والحكم والنبوءة . والإشارة في قوله : { هؤلاء } إلى المشركين من أهل مكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says Qur'an often uses هؤلاء for Quraysh, citing 43:29, and says he found this pattern in his survey though no earlier scholar noted it.
rows.anchor: وقد تقصيت مواقع آي القرآن فوجدته يعبر عن مشركي قريش كثيرا بكلمة ( هؤلاء )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The polytheists’ rejection of earlier prophets follows their rejection of Muhammad; the next verse reports their claim that God sent nothing to any human.
rows.anchor: وكفر المشركين بنبوءة أولئك الأنبياء تابع لكفرهم بمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم ولذلك حكى الله عنهم بعد أنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: وكلنا بها means God enabled others to believe in, observe, and uphold scripture, wisdom, and prophethood; it is a metaphor for entrusting someone to preserve and care for what was entrusted.
rows.anchor: فالتوكيل هنا استعارة ، لأن حقيقة التوكيل إسناد صاحب الشيء تدبير شيئه إلى من يتولى تدبيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The metaphor is apt because a trustee preserves and develops what is in their care; وكلنا also takes على or باء, and its wording concisely answers the waste implied by denial.
rows.anchor: وقد استعير في هذه الآية للتوفيق إلى الإيمان بالنبوءة والكتاب والحكم والنظر في ما تدعو إليه ورعايته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This independent opening repeats the guidance of 6:87 and the scripture, wisdom, and prophethood of 6:89; separating the repetition prepares the consequence فبهداهم اقتده.
rows.anchor: ولأنها وقعت موقع التكرير لمضمون الجملتين اللتين قبلها : جملة { وهديناهم إلى صراط مستقيم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The demonstrative points to those given scripture, wisdom, and prophethood in 6:89; repeating it emphasizes their distinct identity and the importance of the report.
rows.anchor: والمشار إليهم باسم الإشارة هم المشار إليهم بقوله { أولئك الذين آتيناهم الكتاب والحكم والنبوءة }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Definite subject and predicate restrict all human guidance to the named people and their kin, including Adam as humanity’s common ancestor; the restriction is real, while angels’ goodness is innate and excluded.
rows.anchor: لأن المهديين من البشر لا يعدون أن يكونوا أولئك المسمين ومن آبائهم وذرياتهم وإخوانهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse uses the explicit name of God instead of a first-person pronoun to surround the statement with majesty.
rows.anchor: وعدل عن ضمير المتكلم إلى اسم الجلالة الظاهر لقرن هذا الخبر بالمهابة والجلالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: فبهداهم اقتده follows from the completeness of the earlier prophets’ guidance and turns to Muhammad’s share: he is singled out as uniquely ranked, gathering their guidance and completing their virtues across distant ages.
rows.anchor: وفي إفراده بالذكر وترك عده مع الأولين رمز بديع إلى فذاذته وتفرد مقداره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Preposing بهداهم emphasizes that their comprehensive guidance gathers all virtues, so it is not fitting to follow a lesser guide; Muhammad had followed no pre-Islamic hanif, Christian, or Jew.
rows.anchor: ولأجل هذا لم يسبق للنبيء صلى الله عليه وسلم اقتداء بأحد ممن تحنفوا في الجاهلية أو تنصروا أو تهودوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Before prophethood, Zayd ibn Amr offered Muhammad food at Baldah but refused to eat what was sacrificed at their altars, apparently assuming Muhammad followed paganism; God inspired Muhammad to keep silent and preserve the secret, without saying he did not sacrifice to idols.
rows.anchor: فقد لقي النبيء صلى الله عليه وسلم زيد بن عمرو بن نفيلل قبل النبوءة في بلدح وعرض عليه أن يأكل معه من سفرته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad met Waraqa ibn Nawfal and Bahira but followed neither, remaining on the primordial disposition until revelation.
rows.anchor: ولقي ورقة بن نوفل غير مرة بمكة . ولقي بحيرا الراهب . ولم يقتد بأحد من أولئك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الاقتداء derives from القدوة, a model someone imitates; kasra is considered more common by analogy with الإسوة, though al-Misbah says damma is more common, and the lexicons record unusual fatḥa.
rows.anchor: والاقتداء افتعال من القدوة بضم القاف وكسرها وقياسه على الإسوة يقتضي أن الكسر فيه أشهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No simple verb القدوة is attested: the noun appears to yield an iftiʿāl verb like other verbs derived from nouns; قدوة can also be the verbal noun, as in 60:6.
rows.anchor: ولا يعرف له في اللغة فعل مجرد فلم يسمع إلا اقتدى . وكأنهم اعتبروا القدوة اسما جامدا
